executable_actions.on_failure: Block Stage8 repair execution and downstream Stage7 rerun until the permission matrix is checker-accepted.
executable_actions.rationale: Classify the visible repair action classes against the human-agent boundary and current SACG trust barriers without executing repairs or clearing retry requests.

consumes: contaminated artifact.stage6.verification_plan as planning evidence only
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep retry_request.0001 open and keep Stage7/Stage8 promotion blocked; if required verifier contracts cannot be expressed with existing tools, raise a planned_tool or planned_checker capability request for human approval.
executable_actions.rationale: The active earliest blocker is the Stage6 verification-plan/artifact-contract provenance and gate-DAG/tool-protocol contract. This must be repaired in Stage6, not patched downstream in Stage8.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep all active contamination barriers and retry requests in force; do not consume refined Stage6 artifacts downstream as validated inputs.
executable_actions.rationale: SACG barriers may only be reconciled after clean Stage6 replacement artifacts pass their checks; contaminated artifacts cannot be manually promoted.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not proceed to single-layer or board closure; route the failing boundary trace to Stage8 bounded repair with causal localization.
executable_actions.rationale: Once Stage6 verification artifacts are clean, rerun the operator/leaf layer first under the promoted contract; existing Stage7 evidence is contaminated planning/debug evidence only.

executable_actions.on_failure: Localize the earliest single-layer causal boundary and route only that bounded slice to Stage8; keep board/AXI/DDR/Vivado/runtime actions blocked.
executable_actions.rationale: The next verification layer is auto-allowed only after a clean operator-leaf promotion certificate exists; this enforces the three-layer repair loop.

executable_actions.on_failure: Reject or hold the non-bounded repair; continue only with checker-verifiable bounded repairs that preserve existing cross-layer contracts.
executable_actions.rationale: Any repair that changes architecture, pipeline, memory layout, numeric policy, data order, model shape, major template selection, tool-protocol semantics, or ambiguous backend target facts exceeds automatic bounded repair authority.

forbidden_action_blocklist: Do not consume artifacts under active contamination barriers as validated downstream inputs.
Do not manually clear SACG barriers or close retry requests without checker-accepted replacement artifacts.
Do not claim hardware pass from null or not_run real-tool evidence.
Do not modify golden outputs, loosen tolerances, or bypass checkers.
Do not proceed to board/AXI/DDR/Vivado/runtime/bitstream work before clean Stage6, operator-leaf, and single-transformer-layer closure.
Do not perform free-form RTL/template rewrites outside localized, checker-verifiable repair boundaries.
human_approval_request_list: Approval is required before any non-bounded cross-layer change to architecture, pipeline, memory layout, numeric policy, data order, model shape, or major template selection.
Approval is required before changing case_adapter or tool_protocol semantics, changing required real-tool gates, or adding planned_tool/planned_checker capability.
Approval is required before selecting ambiguous backend/app-shell targets or performing backend recovery based on uncertain board evidence.
observations: The boundary review is limited to the supplied summaries and named constraints; detailed Stage8 repair-plan rows were not visible, so classifications are expressed as bounded action classes rather than silent assumptions about omitted rows.

Manual clearing of SACG barriers, manual promotion, tolerance loosening, golden-output modification, or checker bypass would break the human-agent trust boundary.

Architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, numeric-policy, data-order, model-shape, or major template changes would invalidate earlier cross-layer assumptions unless explicitly approved and rechecked from the affected stage.
Backend/app-shell target guessing without board materials and real Vivado evidence would risk invalid deployment facts and is blocked until earlier verification hierarchy passes.
